FIX BUG #375: Read-only commands open the journal read-write, creating and migrating the file they came to read

You are fixing exactly one bug from the code-health epic (#330) on branch fix-375-read-only-opens, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text is below and is the whole framing: its "Fix" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Where the issue says the operator rules between options, implement the option the issue recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say in your result notes which option you took so the pull request can ask for the ruling.

RULES
- Scope: fix this bug and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites.
- Tests: add or extend the suite that proves the fix. Assert exact values and exact error variants or text, never is_err() alone. Show every new test binds: make a compiling mutation that removes the fix, run the test and see it fail, restore the fix, and record the failing test name in your notes.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new line and branch reachable by a test. If a branch cannot be reached deterministically, restructure rather than leave it uncovered.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Gates before you report complete, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test for every crate you touched (crate-scoped: cargo test -p <crate>); git diff --check.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#375)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

THE ISSUE (#375), verbatim:

Found by the code-health sweep (epic #330). Verified on `main` at `8da75ed1` (2026-09-25).

## What happens

These read-only commands open the journal with `Store::open`, which **creates the directory and file, switches to WAL, and runs migrations** (`crates/brokkr-store/src/lib.rs:621-635`):

- `costs`
- `inspect`
- `seats`
- `watch` (re-opened every 750 ms while a `brokkr run` writes to the same file)
- `replay`
- `export`
- `runs`
- `compare`

Meanwhile `tui`, `ui`, `ledger`, `transcript` and the multi-hearth `runs` use `open_read_only`. The codebase's own rule, at `crates/brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs:1099-1102`, says a read "must not enable WAL, migrate columns or repair guards".

Reproduce: `brokkr inspect --run x` in an empty directory leaves `.forge/forge.db` behind.

## Why it matters

- Reads mutate state.
- A read against a journal written by a newer engine can migrate it.
- `watch` takes the write path in a polling loop against a live writer.

## Fix

Have each handler declare `Access::{Read, Append}` and open read-only for `Read`. Keep doctor's deliberate read-write probe explicit.

## Acceptance

- Running every read-only verb in an empty directory creates no file. A test covers each verb.
- `watch` against a live journal never opens it read-write.

This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

inputs.option_taken: Access::{Read, Append} declared per handler through one open_journal; doctor's Store::open kept explicit

result.notes:
Fix (commit b17d27bd, signed + DCO, unpushed): crates/brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs adds `enum Access { Read, Append }` and `open_journal(db, access)`. Read = ensure!(db.is_file(), "journal does not exist: <db>; a read never creates one") then Store::open_read_only; Append = Store::open. costs, inspect, seats, watch (initial resolve AND every poll in watch_loop), replay, export, single-hearth runs and compare (compare.rs) declare Access::Read; run, resume, rerun, conclude, operator retry/stop, import and bridge declare Access::Append. doctor.rs keeps Store::open and gains a comment saying the probe is deliberately read-write.

Widened by one site, required for the change to work: the tui's sole-hearth run resolution (resolve_in_hearths) still used Store::open. After export went read-only, machine_proof `brokkr_tui_is_a_listed_read_verb_that_refuses_a_pipe_and_writes_nothing` FAILED ('the whole workspace is untouched'): a diagnostic print showed the read-only export leaves empty forge.db-wal/-shm, and the tui's read-write resolve deleted them on close. resolve_in_hearths is now always read-only; the read_only flag, resolve_in_hearths_with and resolve_in_hearths_read_only are gone (transcript and 3 tests call resolve_in_hearths). After this change the test passes.

One existing expectation changed (needs operator eyes): tests/realms.rs `the_map_chooses_the_journal_for_the_run_and_for_every_read_surface` asserted `runs --db state/other.db` on a MISSING journal exits 0 with an empty fleet, which held only because the read created the file. It now asserts exit 1, empty stdout, stderr 'journal does not exist: state/other.db; a read never creates one', and that state/other.db was not created; the --db-outranks-the-map and not-announced checks are kept. Alternative if preferred: have single-hearth `runs` list an empty fleet for a missing journal without creating it.

Tests (crates/brokkr-cli/src/tests.rs): `every_reading_verb_in_an_empty_directory_refuses_and_creates_nothing` runs all eight verbs with db=<empty tmp>/.forge/forge.db, asserts the exact refusal text per verb and that the directory still has 0 entries. `watch_never_opens_a_live_journal_read_write` keeps a writer Store open, drops the events_append_only_delete guard trigger, runs watch_loop for 2 polls while the writer appends in the sleep hook, and asserts 2 frames and that the guard is still missing (Store::open would repair it).

Mutation checks: (1) with `Access::Read if true => Ok(Store::open(db)?)` both new tests FAILED: every_reading_verb... (left 'run 'x' not found' vs the refusal) and watch_never_opens... ('a poll repaired the guard', left 1 right 0). (2) with compare.rs switched to Access::Append (the last verb in the loop), every_reading_verb... FAILED (left "loading run 'x'"), so the loop reaches every verb. Both mutations were reverted.

Gates run here: cargo fmt --all -- --check OK; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings OK; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --all-features --locked: 32 test binaries 'ok', no FAILED (lib 470 passed); git diff --check OK; cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self OK. No witness digests moved (no test reported one). Pending, not run by me: scripts/coverage-exact.sh (controller runs it; the new ensure! branch is hit by the empty-dir test, and the removed `sole && !read_only` branch no longer exists), bundles/verify compile, workspace-wide cargo test, remote CI.

Follow-ups, not fixed here: (a) other reads still use Store::open: `anchor --check`, `keep-refs plant`, and keep_ref_run (keep-refs list/delete --run). (b) A read-only open of an existing WAL journal leaves empty -wal/-shm sidecars. This is SQLite reader behaviour already shared by tui/ledger/transcript, and the acceptance only covers empty directories. (c) A journal from before the sidecar columns is no longer migrated by these reads; any query that names a missing column now fails instead of upgrading the journal.
